liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out the second set's Shakedown, Terrapin, Mind Left Body Jam and Truckin' as high points; Shakedown is fully developed, ending with a nice scat passage about poking around [25][30]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Reviewer says Bertha made a strong opener, and they were up front at the show [25]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the first set's one standout, as it usually is with Brent [27]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer finds Looks Like Rain very good in a strong first set, with Deal also cranking [30]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Garcia plays some excellent but sloppy leads on Terrapin [27]
- **Mind Left Body Jam** (1 review): The well-known jam out of Space is where the show moves from good to mind-blowing; Truckin', Wharf Rat and Good Lovin' follow well [27]
- **Truckin'** (1 other source): Truckin' leads into a Heaven Help The Fool jam, then Wharf Rat [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mind Left Body Jam**: back after 146 archived shows (761 days) [36]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96181.sbek.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd83-12-30.sbd.dodd.10280.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Clean-sounding soundboard with clear keyboards; playing is smooth, though the reviewer found the energy fairly low [24]
- **gd1983-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32513.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: The soundboard sounds sterile compared with the fine audience recordings available on the archive [32]
- **gd1983-12-30.sen441.andrewf.109129.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: Prefers the audience recording for better balance; soundboards of this era have too much kick drum and Brent, too little Jerry [35]
- **gd1983-12-30.176814.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 150 min [7]

## Around the show

- Attendee traded New Year's Eve tickets for this show, then got another New Year's Eve ticket right after [26]
- Reviewer hears Garcia as raspy and aggressive, as if working something out, bursting to deliver the music [31]
- The encore is placed at the end of the first set to fit the show on two discs [1]
- Calls the San Francisco Civic a great place to hear the Dead [38]
- Reviewer notes the 12-28 show is also awesome, but this one is two nights later [29]
- Reviewer says the audience tapes capture an electricity that the too-sterile soundboard lacks [32]
- Reviewer enjoyed this more than any other show of the New Year's run, finding it more rollicking than NYE [35]
- Uploader says the 30th is another example of a show better than New Year's Eve [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96181.sbek.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLII-S90) [1]. Also: Cassettes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; pitch correction done with help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd83-12-30.sbd.dodd.10280.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR [2]. Also: Soundboard transferred via MC and DAT to CDR by Paul B, seeded to etree by Ernie Dodd [2]
- **gd1983-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32513.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) [3]. Also: Source cassettes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; encore placed at end of first set for two discs [3]
- **gd1983-12-30.sen441.andrewf.109129.flac2496**: transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Sennheiser MD-441's > patched out of Nak 550 > Marantz PMD-340 > Sony UCX-S 90's. FOB 25 feet from stage in center. [6]
- **gd1983-12-30.176814.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [7]. Also: A Nakamichi 700 source from Bob Wagner and Charlie Miller supplies a 0:52 patch in the Drums to Space transition [7]

claims.text: Clean-sounding soundboard with clear keyboards; playing is smooth, though the reviewer found the energy fairly low
Reviewer says Bertha made a strong opener, and they were up front at the show
Reviewer singles out the second set's Shakedown, Terrapin, Mind Left Body Jam and Truckin' as high points
Attendee traded New Year's Eve tickets for this show, then got another New Year's Eve ticket right after
Reviewer calls it the first set's one standout, as it usually is with Brent
Garcia plays some excellent but sloppy leads on Terrapin
The well-known jam out of Space is where the show moves from good to mind-blowing; Truckin', Wharf Rat and Good Lovin' follow well
Reviewer notes the 12-28 show is also awesome, but this one is two nights later
Reviewer finds Looks Like Rain very good in a strong first set, with Deal also cranking
Shakedown is fully developed, ending with a nice scat passage about poking around
Reviewer hears Garcia as raspy and aggressive, as if working something out, bursting to deliver the music
Reviewer says the audience tapes capture an electricity that the too-sterile soundboard lacks
The soundboard sounds sterile compared with the fine audience recordings available on the archive
Reviewer enjoyed this more than any other show of the New Year's run, finding it more rollicking than NYE
Prefers the audience recording for better balance; soundboards of this era have too much kick drum and Brent, too little Jerry
Cassettes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; pitch correction done with help from Joe B. Jones
The encore is placed at the end of the first set to fit the show on two discs
Soundboard transferred via MC and DAT to CDR by Paul B, seeded to etree by Ernie Dodd
Truckin' leads into a Heaven Help The Fool jam, then Wharf Rat
Uploader says the 30th is another example of a show better than New Year's Eve
Source cassettes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; encore placed at end of first set for two discs
Scott Wiseman supplied source cassettes and transfer, coordinated by Charlie Miller
A Nakamichi 700 source from Bob Wagner and Charlie Miller supplies a 0:52 patch in the Drums to Space transition
Calls the San Francisco Civic a great place to hear the Dead
